m.description:
The number of bits. The more bits per expected entry, the lower the false positive probability.

@see #requiredM

k.description:
The number of hash functions to use. The more hash functions, the lower the false positive probability.

@see #requiredK

title:
The interface of a generic Bloom filter. This is a way to maintain a fixed-size hash of a large number of objects.
However, it is probabilistic in the sense that it may have false positives (but not false negatives).

Traditional terminology for Bloom filters:
 - _m_ bits of data are stored (space required)
 - _k_ hash functions (time required)
 - _n_ the number of values entered
 - _X_ the number of bits that are set
 - _ε_ the false positive probability

The choice of _m_ and _k_ are interrelated, see the Wikipedia page below for more info. The functions
#requiredM and #requiredK may be helpful.

This type is abstract because the actual hash function must be specified by sub-types. This could either be using
_k_ separate hash functions or a smaller number combined in _k_ ways.

This type has an implementation in all three languages so it can be used for client/server communications without
the need to remote. Sub-types should do the same.

@var V the type of values to hash
@see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloom_filter
name: BloomFilter
